title: Searches over 125 s fail with Cloudflare 524: call DataForSEO in queued mode with polling
description:
## Problem

Since de933f7 (deployed 2026-11-24 14:11 UTC), every request sends `resolve_goto_urls` and `resolve_poisoned_results` to
DataForSEO's Live endpoint. With both on, Live requests took 105 to 140 s in testing.

Cloudflare cuts off a Worker's outbound `fetch` when the remote server sends nothing for 125 s, and returns 524. This is
the Proxy Read Timeout in Cloudflare's connection limits
(https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/reference/connection-limits/). Only Enterprise zones can raise it, and a
workers.dev Worker can't. api.dataforseo.com is not on Cloudflare (it serves `Server: nginx` from Hetzner addresses), so
the limit is on our side.

Evidence, production paid test on 2026-11-25 against version 7daeb037 (commit c776692), "best running shoes", US,
depth 10:
- Both endpoints returned HTTP 502 `dataforseo_error` after 125.2 s.
- The body had `"dataforseo_status": 524` and `"dataforseo_body": "error code: 524\n"`.
- The csvkey was accepted (philomena's RUSTY_TOOLS_CSVKEY), and the health, auth and validation checks passed.
- Under `wrangler dev`, the same kind of request completed in 138 s (standard) and 105 s (.ai), so the cutoff exists
  only on Cloudflare's network.

Cloudflare's Workers limits page says "There is no set time limit on individual subrequests". That does not hold for a
fetch to an external server. PRD section 4.6 repeats the claim and must be corrected.

DataForSEO probably still charges for a task whose response Cloudflare cut off. philomena retries failed calls up to
3 times (MAX_ATTEMPTS), and its 120 s client timeout fails these calls even earlier (bead bd-fbm-epic-2fnbw in
philomena).

## Mitigation in place

- 2026-11-25T11:30:01Z: `wrangler rollback` to version 7a88f823-2888-47b4-ba66-666f88b4fbde. That is the May code:
  worker 0.8, no `resolve_goto_urls`, no `resolve_poisoned_results`, and no depth check in the Worker.
  The version it replaced was 7daeb037-0ab9-4a96-a720-b04b095caaf5.
- Verified after the rollback: standard endpoint 200 in 8.4 s, .ai 200 in 3.3 s, both status 20000.
- **Any push to `main` redeploys the 524-prone code.** Workers Builds deploys every push, and it has no
  commit-message skip (`[skip ci]` is documented for Pages only). Do not push `main` until this fix lands, or roll
  back again right after.

## Fix: queued mode with polling (chosen by the owner on 2026-11-25)

Replace the single Live call with DataForSEO's Standard method inside the same Worker request, so that no single
subrequest comes near 125 s:

1. POST `https://api.dataforseo.com/v3/serp/google/organic/task_post` with the same task fields plus `priority: 2`
   (high). Set `resolve_goto_urls: true` explicitly: its default is `true` for priority 1 but `false` for priority 2.
   DataForSEO says it adds up to 40 s to high-priority tasks, with a maximum turnaround of 260 s.
2. Poll `GET /v3/serp/google/organic/task_get/advanced/{id}` until the task is finished, or `{id}.ai` when
   `ai_optimized` is true. On 2026-11-25 a free request confirmed that task_get accepts the `.ai` suffix and answers
   in the `.ai` shape (`id`, `status_code`, `status_message`, `items`). Poll every ~10 s or so: Workers Free allows
   50 subrequests per invocation. Look up which task statuses mean "not ready yet" (40601 Task Handed and 40602 Task
   in Queue, to be confirmed in DataForSEO's error list) and treat everything else as final.
3. Give the whole request an overall deadline (about 280 s) and return 504 `dataforseo_timeout` when it passes.
4. Compare the task_get/advanced response with the live/advanced one (for example `data.function` and `path`).
   rusty-serp passes responses through verbatim, so callers such as philomena's adapter need to be told about any
   difference.
5. Before switching production, confirm on Cloudflare (the `rusty-serp-staging` Worker or a version preview) that a
   Worker can still answer its client after more than 125 s. The 524 applies to the Worker's own outbound request;
   the client side of the connection is not yet verified.
6. Update the README and PRD: request flow, flag table, section 4.6 (timeouts and the subrequest claim above), and the
   cost tables. Standard pricing differs from Live: high priority costs more than normal priority, and the
   `load_async_ai_overview` surcharge is $0.0006 in Standard. Take the per-page prices from DataForSEO's pricing page.
7. Unit tests for the task_post payload (priority, all three flags, both location types) and for the polling status
   handling.

## Acceptance

- `cargo check`, `clippy -D warnings`, `fmt --check`, `test` and `ubs` pass.
- A Cloudflare-hosted test (staging or preview) completes a request that takes more than 125 s end to end.
- After the push to `main`: a production paid smoke test (prod_smoke.py --live) passes on both endpoints. That means
  HTTP 200, status 20000, all three flags echoed in the standard response, and no `google.com/goto` links.
- The README and PRD match the new behavior. philomena's bead bd-fbm-epic-2fnbw gets a comment with the new timing and
  any response-shape differences.
close_reason: Completed. commit=f7f7940 (code), aae738d + 0c7f096 (docs). Production serves Worker version 3f738562 (from f7f7940, deployed 2026-11-25 12:01Z). Tests: cargo check/clippy -D warnings (native + wasm32)/fmt/test (5 passed); UBS 5.5.26 no criticals (findings triaged as error-builder unwrap pattern, compile-time asserts, test code, false positives). Cloudflare probe Worker answered its client after 150 s and 200 s. wrangler dev: std 200 in 144.9 s, .ai 200 in 163.3 s. Staging Worker: std 200 in 170.3 s, .ai 200 in 157.0 s. Production paid smoke test: std 200 in 186.2 s (status 20000, priority 2 and all three flags echoed, cost 0.0024), .ai 200 in 161.8 s (status 20000, 14 items), 0 google.com/goto links in both. philomena bead bd-fbm-epic-2fnbw updated (philomena 932eabf5); its adapter already waits 300 s (a359aa69).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Follow-up after closing (2026-11-25), commit 5dc1f48, from a fresh review of the polling code:

- Each task_get request now has a 10 s limit (AbortSignal.timeout, body included). Before, one hung result request could hold the Worker's answer up to 125 s past the 280 s deadline, past the 300 s client timeout. Worst case is now about 290 s; a compile-time check keeps 10 s of margin. task_post keeps no limit of its own (abandoning it could leave a paid task without its ID; Cloudflare's 125 s cutoff bounds it).
- A task_get response with a top-level status_code of 50000 or higher now counts as a failed request and is retried (three in a row -> 502 dataforseo_error). DataForSEO sends server errors with HTTP 200, so before, a passing hiccup on the free result request ended the call and discarded a paid task.
- Status codes are read into a small struct instead of a full serde_json::Value: 1.3 ms against 13 ms for a 1.9 MB result in a native benchmark (Workers Free allows 10 ms CPU per request).

Evidence: 7 unit tests pass; clippy -D warnings clean (native and wasm32); fmt clean; UBS 5.5.26 no criticals. workerd probe: AbortSignal.timeout(3000) aborts a stalled header and a stalled body at 3.0 s. Local wrangler dev: std 200 in 151.1 s, .ai 200 in 144.8 s. Production version 300efaf8 (Workers Builds success for 5dc1f48): free checks pass; std 200 in 180.3 s (cost 0.0024, priority 2, all three flags echoed), .ai 200 in 174.6 s; status 20000 and 0 goto links on both.

title: Upgrade worker and worker-build to 0.9 and pin worker-build in the build command
description:
## Problem

The Cloudflare build command in `wrangler.toml` installs worker-build without a version:

    cargo install -q worker-build && worker-build --release

Since worker-build 0.9.0 was published, that command builds nothing for this project:

- **worker-build 0.9.0** (latest on crates.io, checked 2026-11-24) refuses the `worker` crate the project uses:
  `Unsupported version worker@0.8.3, expected at least worker@0.9.0`.
- **worker-build 0.8.7** (the global install on this VPS) fails at the wasm-bindgen step: the wasm-bindgen CLI rejects the
  `--force-enable-abort-handler` flag it passes. Cargo.lock has wasm-bindgen 0.2.122.
- **worker-build 0.8.3** is the only version that currently builds this project. It was used for the local `wrangler dev`
  test of `resolve_goto_urls` on 2026-11-24.

Effect: the next push to `main` starts a Cloudflare build that will almost certainly fail, so production stays on the old code.
The `resolve_goto_urls` commits 74918f1, f31d0b1 and b682cb7 are waiting on this. `wrangler.toml` now has `name = "rusty-serp"`,
so a successful build deploys straight to production.

## Work

1. Read the workers-rs changelog for worker 0.9.0 and list breaking changes that touch this code: `Request`, `Response`,
   `Headers`, `RequestInit`, `Fetch`, `Env::secret`, `Url`, and the `#[event(fetch)]` entry point.
2. In `Cargo.toml`, change `worker = "0.8"` to `"0.9"`. Run `cargo update -p worker`, then fix any compile errors.
3. Pin the build tool in the `wrangler.toml` build command, so the next worker-build release can't break builds again:
   `cargo install -q worker-build --version <0.9.x> --locked`.
4. Update the PRD to match: the build command in §5.2 and `worker = "0.8"` in §5.3.
5. Build with the pinned worker-build, run `wrangler dev`, and smoke-test it:
   - `/health` returns 200
   - a wrong csvkey returns 401
   - depth 201 returns 400 `invalid_depth`
   - one live call per endpoint (standard and `.ai`) returns status 20000 with no `google.com/goto` links

   Run wrangler under nvm Node, not the Bun-run wrangler on PATH, which can't forward requests in dev.
   On this VPS, run the Bun-installed wrangler package (4.167.0) with Node, not Bun:
   ~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.22.3/bin/node ~/.bun/install/global/node_modules/wrangler/bin/wrangler.js
   The nvm-global wrangler is 4.96.0, too old for worker 0.9 (every request returns 500).

Fallback if the 0.9 upgrade stalls and a deploy is needed first: pin `--version 0.8.3 --locked` in the build command.
This is a stopgap, not the fix.

## Acceptance

- `worker` 0.9.x is in Cargo.lock, and the build command pins worker-build with `--version` and `--locked`.
- These all pass: `cargo check --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`,
  `cargo test`, and `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. `ubs` has been run on the changed files.
- `worker-build --release` succeeds with the pinned version, and the `wrangler dev` smoke tests above pass.
- The Cloudflare build for the pushed commit succeeds, and production `/health` answers.
close_reason: Completed. Pushed de933f7; Workers Builds check 'Workers Builds: rusty-serp' succeeded (build c06500c6-c760-47b1-8c0e-302f55640778); production now serves version dae7225e-5da4-4d2e-8786-a3776c619c29 (100%). Production checks: GET/HEAD /v1/health 200, no csvkey 400, wrong csvkey 401, GET /v1/serp 405, so worker 0.9's tracing APIs exist on the production runtime. Local: check/clippy/fmt/test pass; worker-build 0.9.0 --locked builds; wrangler dev live calls passed. Rollback target if needed: 7a88f823-2888-47b4-ba66-666f88b4fbde.

comments.author: claude-opus
comments.text:
Local verification, 2026-11-24 (before push):

- Cargo.toml worker 0.8 -> 0.9; Cargo.lock worker/worker-macros/worker-sys 0.9.0, wasm-bindgen 0.2.130. No source changes needed.
- The 0.8.4-0.9.0 release notes list no breaking change to the APIs used here (Request, Response, Headers, RequestInit, Fetch, Env::secret).
- cargo check --all-targets, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings, cargo fmt --check, cargo test (2 passed): all pass.
  cargo +stable check and clippy --target wasm32-unknown-unknown: pass.
- From an empty root, `cargo install worker-build --version 0.9.0 --locked` installs 0.9.0.
- `worker-build --release` (0.9.0, stable): 374 KB wasm.
  It warns that `target_features` is missing because of strip = true. That is harmless: wasm-bindgen 0.2.130 then infers
  reference types from the externref exports (cli-support/src/lib.rs, around line 425).
- `wrangler dev` (4.167.0, compat date 2026-05-03): the worker loads with worker 0.9's tracing hooks.
  - health GET and HEAD return 200
  - a missing csvkey returns 400; a wrong csvkey returns 401
  - invalid JSON returns 400; depth 201 returns 400 invalid_depth
  - GET /v1/serp returns 405
  - live standard call: 200 in 110.0 s, task status 20000, data.resolve_goto_urls=true, 0 google.com/goto links, cost $0.002
  - live .ai call: 200 in 85.7 s, status 20000, 0 google.com/goto links
  - no panics or exceptions in the dev log
- Wrangler 4.96.0 (the copy in the nvm v22.22.3 globals) failed to start because of local .wrangler state written by a newer
  workerd. That is unrelated to the build; it ran fine on 4.167.0.

Remaining before close: the Cloudflare build for the pushed commit succeeds, and production /v1/health answers.

comments.author: claude-opus
comments.text:
Review pass, 2026-11-24. This corrects the previous comment.

- The previous comment was wrong to call the Wrangler 4.96.0 failure unrelated. With fresh local state, 4.96.0 (workerd 1.20260529.1)
  loads the worker 0.9 build, but every request returns 500 with `Uncaught Error: Critical error`.
  worker 0.9 runs each handler under the runtime's trace span, using `tracing.getActiveSpan` and `tracing.withActiveSpan`.
  workerd 1.20260529.1 has neither method; 1.20261123.1 (Wrangler 4.167.0) has both.
  In workerd's source, `withActiveSpan` was added on 2026-11-05 (commit a14d809f6). It is a plain JSG_METHOD with no compatibility flag,
  so our compatibility date of 2026-05-03 doesn't matter. README and PRD section 9.3 now say local dev needs a current Wrangler.
  Production runs Cloudflare's current runtime, so it should have both methods. The post-push /v1/health check confirms it.
- worker-build checks `^<its minor>.0` against the lockfile (worker-build src/lockfile.rs), so 0.9.0 accepts worker 0.9.x only.
  The wrangler.toml comment and the PRD now say so, and explain why the pin is exact rather than `^0.9`
  (worker-build 0.8.7 broke against the locked wasm-bindgen 0.2.122).
- UBS project scan (5.5.26, --only=rust): exit 1. Its only critical was the cargo-deny phase: the global cargo-deny 0.17.0 can't parse
  CVSS 4.0 advisories. cargo-deny 0.20.2 (rusty-jev/.tools/bin) found two advisories, both already in the lockfile before this upgrade:
  - RUSTSEC-2026-0592: url 2.5.8 stack overflow in Url::origin(). Fixed with `cargo update -p url --precise 2.5.9`
    (also form_urlencoded 1.2.3). 2.5.9 additionally fixes quadratic `..` parsing, which matters because the Worker parses
    untrusted request URLs.
  - RUSTSEC-2026-0543: chrono is unmaintained, with no safe upgrade. It is a required dependency of worker 0.9.0, so it is left as is.
  The remaining UBS warnings are pre-existing patterns in unchanged source (unwrap on json_error and similar); no Rust source changed here.
- On this VPS, "wrangler under nvm Node" (from the description) needs one more detail. The nvm-global wrangler
  (~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.22.3/lib/node_modules/wrangler) is 4.96.0 and too old.
  Use ~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.22.3/bin/node ~/.bun/install/global/node_modules/wrangler/bin/wrangler.js (4.167.0).
- Production is still on the code from May. The last Workers Builds check run succeeded on 3149e44 (2026-05-23), before worker-build 0.9.0.
- Re-verified on the final lockfile (url 2.5.9):
  - check, clippy -D warnings (native and wasm32/stable), fmt, and test (2 passed) all pass
  - the pinned worker-build 0.9.0 builds a 374 KB wasm
  - wrangler dev 4.167.0 passes all 7 health, auth, validation and method checks
  - live standard call: 200 in 89.6 s, 20000, data.resolve_goto_urls=true, 0 goto links
  - live .ai call: 200 in 91.2 s, 20000, 14 items, 0 goto links
  - no errors in the dev log
- Rerunning `cargo install worker-build --version 0.9.0 --locked` when 0.9.0 is already installed exits 0, so a cached toolchain is fine.
